name: Titanium.Network.TCPSocket
summary:
The TCPSocket instance returned from [Titanium.Network.createTCPSocket](api:Titanium.Network#createTCPSocket).  This object
represents a socket which either listens locally on the device for connections,
or connects to a remote machine.
description: Sockets are nontrivial; it is recommended that anyone using them be familiar with the basics of BSD sockets.  All sockets use TCP connections, and are asynchronous for read operations, so your program should be ready to receive 'read' events at any point.  Socket references cannot be transferred to socket objects, and vice-versa - socket references are an internal mechanism which is used only to determine which sockets to send data to and read data from.  For listening sockets, it is highly recommended that you use the <Titanium.Network.INADDR_ANY> constant as the host name.  If a window containing a socket is closed, the socket MUST be closed also unless you intend to continue to receive data, otherwise the socket will consume resources (and potentially cause conflicts with opening the window again, if a listener) until the program is restarted.  Be aware of the differences between the listen() and connect() functions; attempting to use one when you mean the other may result in errors, unpredictable behavior, or both.

properties.name: hostName
properties.summary: the host name to connect to.  Must be <Titanium.Network.INADDR_ANY> or an identifier for the local device in order to listen

properties.name: isValid
properties.summary: whether or not the socket is valid

properties.name: stripTerminator
properties.summary: strip terminating null character when sending string data; default is false

methods.name: connect
methods.summary: connect the socket to a TCP server

methods.name: listen
methods.summary: set up the socket to receive connections

methods.name: write
methods.summary: write data to the socket, if the mode is WRITE_MODE or READ_WRITE_MODE

parameters.name: data
parameters.summary: either a string or blob object representing the data to be transferred

parameters.name: sendTo
parameters.summary: the socket reference to send the data to.  Default is to send to all connected sockets

events.name: read
events.summary: new data was read off the socket

properties.name: from
properties.summary: the reference for the socket that data was retrieved from

properties.name: data
properties.summary: a blob representing the data read, can be interpreted via toString

properties.name: error
properties.summary: Error message, if any returned. May be undefined.

properties.name: code
properties.summary:
Error code.
If the error was generated by the operating system, that system's error value
is used. Otherwise, this value will be -1.
